transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-02
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Donnell (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Aaron Kessler (CTO - Solace), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Victor Huang (Platform)
Notes/Links: redwood-poc-benchmark.xlsx, security-pack.zip, demo link (to be scheduled)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. quick agenda — scope success criteria, workload sizing and then integration planning (SDKs, openai-compatible endpoints, function calling). sound good?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Yeah that works. thanks Maya.
00:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): sorry I'm joining from transit, audio might be a bit fuzzy.
00:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): no worries priya, we can recap. so to start, can you walk us through what success looks like for the POC? we want to make sure the tests map to your product KPIs.
00:45 Speaker 4 (Aaron): sure. our main goal is to reduce triage time for incoming diagnostic reports by 40% and surface the top-3 likely issues with confidence scores. also latency matters — sub-500ms per inference for the single-request path would be ideal for interactive use.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Liam): ok that's helpful. are you expecting synchronous chat-like calls or batch processing of reports?
01:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): both, really. batch for nightly ingest and synchronous for clinician-facing UI. batch volume is about 100k reports/day, average 600 tokens per report after extraction; peak concurrent sync QPS is around 60-80 in EU timezone.
01:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): good. that gives us a baseline. for the POC we typically run a throughput benchmark for batch and a latency SLO test for sync. we'll also run quality evals against your labeled set to hit the 40% triage reduction target.
01:50 Speaker 2 (Liam): quick note — since you mentioned clinician UI, does HIPAA compliance or specific data residency matter?
01:58 Speaker 4 (Aaron): yes HIPAA applies. we need SOC2 plus proof of encryption at rest with customer KMS, and ideally private VPC peering for any dedicated environment.
02:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): understood. Redwood supports VPC/private deployments and KMS/HSM integrations; we'll include architecture and SOC2 in the security pack.
02:20 Speaker 3 (Priya): perfect. on the integration side, can you explain the OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDK story?
02:30 Speaker 2 (Liam): sure. Redwood exposes OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints (same request/response shape for models), plus official SDKs in Python and JS. we also provide a higher-level SDK that supports streaming, function-calling semantics, structured output enforcement (we can validate JSON schema), and automatic retries/prefix caching.
02:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): and for function/tool calling — we support the style where model outputs can invoke pre-registered tools (like a DB retriever, run SQL, or hit an internal service). we can show a demo wired to a retrieval tool and a small lambda to fetch patient metadata.
03:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): ok that aligns with our architecture. how do you handle privacy for tool calls — do those payloads go through Redwood, or can they be routed to our VPC directly?
03:22 Speaker 2 (Liam): for private deployments, tool calls can be executed within your VPC; for hosted mode we have strict egress policies and can use customer-managed scopes and audit logs. payload routing is configurable per-route.
03:35 Speaker 4 (Victor): good. what about model variants and quantized weights — are they available for lower-cost inference?
03:42 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes. we maintain a model catalog with verified performance profiles. for the POC we'll recommend an ensemble: a small quantized candidate for low-latency, and a larger baseline for quality checks. our Optimize tooling will suggest quantization and batching settings by workload.
04:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): let's talk benchmarks — what do you need from us?
04:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): we can provide 200 sample reports (redacted) and a labeled set for evaluation metrics.
04:16 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect. we'll run the tokenized workload estimator (we'll send the template) to confirm tokens/day, tokens per request, and expected QPS. for batch benchmarks we'll run a nightly throughput job to measure cost/tokens and for sync we'll run p99 latency and tail latency tests.
04:34 Speaker 2 (Liam): practical note: for sync latency testing, please share the expected prompt size (you said ~600 tokens) and the average expected generated tokens — that impacts per-request latency and memory/KV cache sizes.
04:45 Speaker 3 (Priya): generation is usually short — 40-120 tokens.
04:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): good. so preliminary numbers: 100k reports/day * 600 tokens = ~60M input tokens/day plus gen tokens. we'll include cost estimates and show dedicated vs hosted TCO.
05:05 Speaker 4 (Aaron): timeline question: how long for the POC?
05:09 Speaker 1 (Maya): typical is 4-6 weeks: week 0 prep + security signoff, week 1 integration and dataset handoff, weeks 2-3 benchmarking and iterative tuning, week 4 evaluation and handoff. can flex if you want an accelerated 3-week pilot.
05:25 Speaker 3 (Priya): 4 weeks sounds reasonable. we need to align stakeholders though — can you include a short rollup for the execs?
05:32 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we'll send a 1-page exec summary with success metrics and go/no-go criteria.
05:38 Speaker 2 (Liam): technical question from my side — how will you authenticate? do you prefer API keys or SAML-backed tokens?
05:45 Speaker 4 (Victor): we use SAML for everything internally, but for the POC we can accept scoped API keys if they expire and are auditable.
05:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): fine. we'll support short-lived API keys and show SSO/SAML integration options for production.
05:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): about structured output — can Redwood enforce the model to output a fixed JSON schema with typed fields and confidence?
06:06 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes. we have a structured output enforcement layer; you can provide a JSON schema. the runtime will validate and attempt to recover or return a parse failure with token span. we also support function-style responses that map to typed objects.
06:20 Speaker 4 (Aaron): nice. and can we get an example of tool-calling + retrieval? that is key for citing past records.
06:27 Speaker 2 (Liam): absolutely — Liam: we'll build a demo that shows query -> retrieval -> tool call to fetch patient history -> structured JSON output. should be in the lab demo.
06:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok moving into risk/concerns — Priya?
06:44 Speaker 3 (Priya): main concerns are PHI handling, audit logs, and the ability to run in our VPC with customer-managed KMS. also cost — our finance team will want estimated $/1000 tokens and committed pricing tiers.
06:59 Speaker 1 (Maya): we will include committed pricing for Dedicated capacity and estimate per-token for hosted. also show the effect of batching and prefix caching on unit cost.
07:12 Speaker 4 (Victor): any SLA on latency or availability for Dedicated?
07:16 Speaker 2 (Liam): dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and configurable latency targets; we'll propose a profile that meets your p99 latency needs for the sync path.
07:25 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick clarification on metrics for success: triage reduction >=40% on labeled set; p95 latency <=350ms for sync (target); batch throughput sufficient to process 100k/day within a 2-hour window for nightly jobs. agree?
07:40 Speaker 4 (Aaron): yes that maps to our needs.
07:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok since we have about 40 minutes left in the call, Liam and Rina will run a brief tech walk-through and show a small code snippet for the OpenAI-compatible call and function-calling.
07:55 Speaker 2 (Liam): (screen-share) here's a curl example — note the endpoint is compatible: POST /v1/chat/completions with model param. body shows messages array and function_calls param. the response shape matches OpenAI standard with choices[].message.content or choices[].message.function_call.
08:18 Speaker 2 (Liam): (reads) example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1.2-quant\", \"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Summarize patient note\"}],\"functions\":[{\"name\":\"get_patient\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"patient_id\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}]}'
08:44 Speaker 3 (Rina): in the SDK (python) it's one call: client.chat.completions.create(..., function_call={\"name\":\"get_patient\"}) and you get back function_call.name and arguments as JSON. we can show schema enforcement too.
09:00 Speaker 2 (Liam): streaming is supported — for UI we can stream tokens with SSE or websockets, and we expose server-side hooks for bookkeeping and cost attribution.
09:10 Speaker 4 (Victor): good. about throttling and rate limits — can we set per-route throttles so clinician UI isn't impacted by a background batch?
09:19 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes per-route policies, quotas, and prioritized routing. you can set an SLA route for clinician UI with reserved capacity in Dedicated.
09:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): wrapping to logistics — we'll send the benchmark template, security pack, and schedule the lab demo. recap on action items at the end.
09:40 Speaker 4 (Aaron): sounds good, thanks.

(Transcript continues with back-and-forth about scheduling and minor clarifications; omitted for brevity)

50:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap — action items: Maya will send benchmark template and exec 1-pager; Liam will prepare demo for function-calling; Priya will send sample data; Victor will confirm security POC contact. we'll aim to have the lab demo before 2027-06-09.
51:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): agreed. thanks everyone.
51:14 Speaker 4 (Aaron): thanks, bye.
51:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): thanks all, bye.
